newsitem.title: RWANDA: Tens of thousands of Hutu refugees flee Zaire fighting.
newsitem.headline: Tens of thousands of Hutu refugees flee Zaire fighting.

text.p: Some 46,000 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees have fled two camps in eastern Zaire where the Zairean army is battling ethnic Tutsis, a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency said on Saturday.

"The populations of both Kagunga and Runingo (camps), some 46,000 refugees, have all moved -- some to Uvira, some into the hills above Uvira, some into banana plantations, and the remainder have dispersed," Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Zaire's neighbour Rwanda, told Reuters.
"Because of difficulty in assessing the area outside Uvira, even normal activities are in question. We have only been able to distribute aid in and around Uvira," he added.
Stromberg said Kagunga had a population of 27,000 refugees before it was attacked by the Tutsis -- known as Banyamulenge -- on Friday while Runingo camp had a total of 19,000.

Fresh fighting erupted around Uvira on Saturday after the Banyamulenge -- ethnic Tutsis who came to Zaire from Rwanda at the end of the 18th century -- attacked Luvengi refugee camp near Uvira. There are 12 refugee camps in the Uvira chain with a population of 220,000 people.
At least 28 civilians have been killed in attacks in Zaire's eastern refugee zone in the fighting, humanitarian sources said on Saturday.

A senior Zairean military commander told Reuters that ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge from Rwanda's army had crossed the border from Burundi on Friday and had targeted civilians living around the village of Kiliba.
"When they arrived they opened fire with light arms on the local population living in villages around Kiliba," he said.
Aid workers in Bukavu said that dead and wounded from Friday's attacks near a sugar factory in Kiliba had been arriving at Uvira, 15 km (10 miles) away.

Zaire is host to hundreds of thousands of Hutu refugees who fled fearing reprisals in Rwanda after the 1994 massacres of minority Tutsis by Hutu hardliners there. Other Hutu refugees fled similar ethnic conflict in Burundi.
The Banyamulenge say they are fighting for their right to Zairean citizenship. They say they are discriminated against by indigenous Zaireans on the basis of language and ethnicity.
Zaire has been reinforcing and rearming troops in the area.
